advisory.finding: test_no_teaching_surface_writes_a_removed_spelling is a fail-open oracle: it asserts `offenders == {}` (absence) but never asserts the scanned/enumerated set is non-empty or that a known teaching surface (e.g. docs/user-guide.md) was actually read. If `_scanned()` silently matches nothing (prefix/filter regression, unexpected git cwd), the assertion passes vacuously — the test cannot distinguish 'no survivors' from 'scanned nothing'.
merged_from: The diff narrows the import exemption so only `from rebar import` is exempt, and `import` is itself a removed spelling, yet test_scan_pattern_matches_invocations_not_imports never asserts the positive case `rebar import <file>` (an invocation NOT preceded by `from `) trips the scan — leaving the exemption boundary under-verified for the one spelling that collides with the exempted keyword.
advisory.suggested_fix: Accumulate the set of scanned relative paths and assert a known surface is present, e.g. `assert "docs/user-guide.md" in scanned`, before `assert offenders == {}`.
